description: Failure-first operational health, bounded reliability signals, logical-interface drill-downs, announce flow, request traces, and structured events for prnsd.

panels.description: Liveness only: LIVE means the daemon published a runtime snapshot within two minutes.
panels.title: Daemon live

panels.description: HEALTHY: no hard runtime failure or engine-capacity degradation in the last 5 minutes. DEGRADED: routes got evicted or a table ran out of room. FAULT: the runtime hit a hard failure. Bounded egress pressure and shedding are expected flow control and do not affect this state. Interface up/down and host problems are shown separately and do not affect it either.

targets.expr: 3 * ((max(last_over_time(prns_runtime_up[2m])) or vector(0)) == bool 0) + ((max(last_over_time(prns_runtime_up[2m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) * clamp_max(2 * (((sum(increase(prns_egress_frames_total{outcome="lane_missing"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_egress_total{outcome=~"lane_missing|ifac_rejected|pacer_expired"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_ingress_total{outcome=~"held_dropped_.*"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_operations_total{outcome!="succeeded"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_resources_failures_total{cause!="cancelled_by_sender"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_closures_total{reason=~"timeout|malformed_rtt"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_interface_mismatches_total[5m])) or vector(0))) > bool 0) + ((((sum(increase(prns_routes_removals_total{cause="evicted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) + ((sum(increase(prns_engine_ignored_packets_total{reason="capacity_exhausted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) + ((sum(increase(prns_resources_admission_events_total{event="rejected"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0)) > bool 0), 2)

panels.title: Operational state

panels.description: Actionable hard-failure signals in the last five minutes. Bounded egress pressure, lane shedding, and pacer shedding are excluded. Related counters can describe the same incident, so this is a signal count rather than a unique-incident count.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(prns_egress_frames_total{outcome="lane_missing"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_egress_total{outcome=~"lane_missing|ifac_rejected|pacer_expired"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_announces_ingress_total{outcome=~"held_dropped_.*"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_operations_total{outcome!="succeeded"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_resources_failures_total{cause!="cancelled_by_sender"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_closures_total{reason=~"timeout|malformed_rtt"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(prns_links_interface_mismatches_total[5m])) or vector(0)))

panels.title: Hard signals · 5m

panels.description: How many pressure signals fired in the last 5 minutes: route eviction and table capacity. Egress lane shed does not count here, it is normal backpressure. Interface up/down and crypto work deferrals do not count either.

targets.expr: (((sum(increase(prns_routes_removals_total{cause="evicted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) + ((sum(increase(prns_engine_ignored_packets_total{reason="capacity_exhausted"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0) + ((sum(increase(prns_resources_admission_events_total{event="rejected"}[5m])) or vector(0)) > bool 0))

panels.title: Degraded conditions

panels.description: Persistence, identity, configuration, interface-start, and shared-instance failures from structured daemon events.
panels.title: Host faults · 5m

panels.description: Connected or degraded interfaces are online.
panels.title: Interfaces

panels.description: Non-zero signals from the last five minutes. Blue bars are expected bounded egress pressure or shedding and identify the affected logical interface. Red bars are genuine hard failures. Related counters can describe the same incident.

panels.title: Pressure and failure breakdown · 5m

panels.description: Counts from the last five minutes. Blue egress shedding is expected bounded flow control and does not change Operational state. Yellow engine, route, and resource-capacity events indicate degradation.
panels.title: Bounded-capacity activity · 5m

panels.description: Every logical interface not currently Connected, by name and exact state. This is informational and does not lower Operational state.

targets.expr: (max by (interface, interface_kind, interface_origin) (prns_interface_state) != 1) or on() label_replace(label_replace(((count(max by (interface, interface_kind, interface_origin) (prns_interface_state) != 1) or vector(0)) == 0) + 1, "interface", "All interfaces connected", "__name__", ".*"), "interface_origin", "n/a", "interface", "All interfaces connected")

panels.title: Interface attention

panels.description: Settled caller-visible failures by bounded operation and exact outcome.
panels.title: Operation failures

panels.description: Incoming resource failures and abnormal link closure or interface-mismatch signals. Peer-requested closures and sender cancellations are excluded here.
panels.title: Resource and link failures

panels.description: Malformed, invalid, refused, rate-limited, and capacity-exhausted ingress. Routine duplicate, superseded, not-for-us, and loop-prevention outcomes are intentionally excluded.
panels.title: Rejected ingress and capacity

panels.description: Total data sent and received since the daemon started. Same numbers as prnsd status --totals.
panels.title: Traffic since up

panels.description: Current engine and interface-pacer pressure. Deferred work is retained, not lost; age shows how long the oldest lane-backpressured announce has waited.
panels.title: Announce pressure

panels.description: How fast the whole node is sending and receiving. Computed from the byte counters, so short bursts always show up.
panels.title: Node traffic

panels.description: How long requests this node sends out itself take, like prnsd probe or a fetch it makes over a link. Measured from tracing spans; every one is recorded. Tempo can only compute this over a window of 3 hours or less.
panels.title: Outbound Request Latency

panels.description: How many requests this node answered in each time slice, like a page fetch from its hosted pages, split by outcome.
panels.title: Inbound Requests

panels.description: Frames skipped because their interface was not online. This is not packet loss and does not lower Operational state; sustained activity identifies where connectivity is absent.
panels.title: Unavailable egress

panels.description: Packets and host commands ingested by the engine, and frames enqueued for egress.
panels.title: Engine throughput

panels.description: Saturation of the offloaded cryptographic worker pool. Sustained depth near the high-water mark or a growing verdict debt means inbound packets are waiting on cryptographic work.
panels.title: Cryptographic queue

panels.description: Cryptographic jobs submitted and completed, with backpressure deferrals when the pool refuses new work.
panels.title: Cryptographic jobs

panels.description: One bounded row per logical interface, including whether it was configured or discovered. Fleet peers roll up beneath their TCP, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, backbone, WebSocket, or shared-instance supervisor.
panels.title: Interface overview

panels.description: How much data each interface moved in the selected time range. Relayed traffic counts as received on one interface and transmitted on another.
panels.title: Busiest interfaces · selected range

panels.description: How fast each selected interface is sending and receiving. Computed from the byte counters, so short bursts always show up.
panels.title: Interface traffic

panels.description: Validated ingress outcomes and egress outcomes for the selected logical interfaces.
panels.title: Interface announce flow

panels.description: Per-interface announce queues, oldest deferred age, and physical-lane occupancy. Lane depth should only be reconsidered when sustained occupancy corroborates deferral age and retries.

targets.expr: 100 * max by (physical_lane, logical_interface) (prns_egress_lane_occupancy{logical_interface=~"$interface"}) / clamp_min(max by (physical_lane, logical_interface) (prns_egress_lane_capacity{logical_interface=~"$interface"}), 1)

panels.title: Interface announce pressure

panels.description: How much data moved in each time slice, one color per interface. Received is above the line, transmitted below. Relayed traffic shows a bar above and a matching bar below at the same moment: that pair implies the likely the path it took. Hover to see the names. Always shows all interfaces, ignoring the filter. Slices are 1 minute zoomed in, wider zoomed out.
panels.title: Relay flow · all interfaces

panels.description: Which interfaces are carrying relayed links right now. A relayed conversation counts on both the interface it comes in on and the one it goes out on, so matching lines are a pair.
panels.title: Transit links by interface

panels.description: Validated announces as they enter the engine, including held and capacity outcomes.
panels.title: Inbound announces

panels.description: Announce frames accepted by outbound interface lanes after any applicable pacing and IFAC masking.
panels.title: Outbound announces

panels.description: Terminal per-interface announce outcomes. Categorical colors distinguish each interface, origin, and outcome series; use the top-level pressure and failure panels for semantic blue/red classification. Deferral and recovery remain pressure lifecycle events, not terminal outcomes.
panels.title: Announce terminal egress outcomes

panels.description: Temporary announce egress pressure. Categorical colors distinguish each interface, origin, and event series. Deferred counts once per announce, retry counts later failed attempts, and recovered confirms eventual lane admission.
panels.title: Announce backpressure

panels.description: Prns-owned announce command outcomes. Shared-client and relay traffic is shown in the outbound panel.
panels.title: Local announce commands

panels.description: Accepted inbound announces grouped by their receiving interface kind.
panels.title: Inbound announce interfaces

panels.description: Announce frames accepted by each outbound interface kind.
panels.title: Outbound announce interfaces

panels.description: Path requests as the engine classifies them: answered from our destinations or route cache, relayed onward, or ignored with the reason.
panels.title: Inbound path requests

panels.description: Relay transmissions of path requests toward other interfaces, one count per target, with per-interface egress throttling shown as rate_limited.
panels.title: Path request relays

panels.description: Unknown-destination discoveries currently awaiting an answer, capped by the recursive table; steady growth means requests are outpacing responses.
panels.title: Pending path discoveries

panels.description: Path requests this node recursed onto the network (recursive or boundary forwarding). Stays at 0 unless an interface opts in via a discovery mode (gateway, access point, roaming, internal) or recursive_prs; anything above 0 deserves a look at the interface config.
panels.title: Recursed path requests · since up

panels.description: Raw packet counts since the daemon started: everything the engine ingested, and every frame enqueued to an outbound lane. The live per-second view is the Engine throughput panel.
panels.title: Packets since up

panels.description: Raw packet flow over time: everything the engine ingests and every frame enqueued to an outbound lane. The load view: announce storms, relay bursts, and quiet hours all show up here first.
panels.title: Packet flow

panels.description: Warnings and errors retain their structured event names and diagnostic fields.
panels.title: Warnings and errors

panels.description: Searchable structured lifecycle and diagnostic events from prnsd stderr.
panels.title: Recent prnsd events

panels.description: Active Resource buffer occupancy against each configured directional budget. Fixed embedded stores report occupied slot capacity against their compile-time budget; host stores report exact active bytes against the configured heap budget.
panels.title: Resource buffer memory

panels.description: Active transfer rows and pending inbound offers, alongside admission events. Expiration and rejection are separate events: an expired offer also emits the standard Resource cancellation and therefore increments both.
panels.title: Resource admission
